newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway examines report officers bought child sex.
newsitem.headline: Norway examines report officers bought child sex.

text.p: Norwegian military police have launched an investigation into allegations that Norwegian officers serving under the United Nations flag bought child sex in Angola, officials said on Friday.
Lieutenant Roar Thon, head of the military investigation group in Oslo, said the enquiries would cover all Norwegian officers serving in the U.N. observer corps in Angola between 1992 and 1994.
"There are no specific allegations against specific officers. We will question all officers in Angola in that timeframe. That includes just over 20 officers," Thon told Reuters.
Authorities initiated the investigation after Norwegian journalist Tomm Kristiansen said he had witnessed Norwegian U.N. personnel exploiting prostitutes, including children, in Africa.
"Travelling in African countries I have myself seen how Norwegian U.N. personnel have participated in the local sex market," Kristiansen told the daily Aftenposten.

"I never asked for birth certificates and don't know the age of the girls but I am certain that several of them were under the age of 16...This is also about morals, about how Norwegian soldiers relate to people in the Third World," he said.
